# PreloadingUsageCorrectness

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="tip" text="quick-fix" /> 

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs) · PhpStorm name: `PreloadingUsageCorrectnessInspection`

In an opcache preload script, including files with `require`/`include`
executes them, which can fail on unresolved dependencies (PHP bug #78918).
`opcache_compile_file()` only compiles and caches the file, which is what a
preload script usually wants.

## Example

File `preload.php`:

::: code-group

```php{2,3,4} [Before]
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/src/Kernel.php';
include_once($base . 'helpers.php');
require_once ( 'vendor/autoload.php' );
$map = require 'classmap.php';
return include 'tail.php';
```

```php [After fix]
<?php
opcache_compile_file(__DIR__ . '/src/Kernel.php');
opcache_compile_file($base . 'helpers.php');
opcache_compile_file('vendor/autoload.php');
$map = require 'classmap.php';
return include 'tail.php';
```

:::

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use opcache_compile_file() in a preload script instead of require.</li>
<li>line 3: Use opcache_compile_file() in a preload script instead of include_once.</li>
<li>line 4: Use opcache_compile_file() in a preload script instead of require_once.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "PreloadingUsageCorrectness": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore PreloadingUsageCorrectness

/**
 * @noinspection PreloadingUsageCorrectnessInspection
 */
```
